Discover the Secrets Waiting Inside Norček Industries in We Were Here Tomorrow
A new adventure is on the horizon for co-op fans. In the latest trailer for We Were Here Tomorrow , we offer a closer look at some of the strange places and asymmetric puzzles awaiting players when the game launches for XBOX Series X|S this October.

Norček is researching something that could have enormous consequences for the world. What exactly lies beyond it, and why Norček is so interested in the rift, are questions we want you to discover for yourselves.

Every Wednesday, dive into the Indie Select Hub — your gateway to a fresh, curated indie collection plus four themed spotlights that rotate weekly! You can always find this collection hub in the XBOX Store and on XBOX.com/IndieSelects.
The grill’s cooling down, school is starting up, and the weather is changing. You know what that means: it’s time for a seasonal refresh. So, before you go shopping for your new fit, let’s make sure we also add some bold indie originals to your gaming queue.  We’re thinking: classic foundations but with some new ideas thrown in the mix.
This season, the ID@Xbox team has handpicked six Indie Selects that reinvent familiar genres with unforgettable worlds, creative mechanics, and unique perspectives. Every game delivers a distinctive premise, whether it’s managing superheroes, driving a magical truck, surviving nightmares, building kingdoms, or fighting in massive wars. Here’s what we’ve got for you this month (in no particular order):
What happens when a superhero loses the thing that makes him super? Apparently, he gets a desk job. Dispatch takes the superhero formula and flips it completely. You play as Robert Robertson, better known as Mecha Man. After losing his mech suit, Robert joins the Superhero Dispatch Network, where instead of saving the day himself, he’s responsible for sending others to do it. The problem? His team consists largely of former supervillains trying to become heroes. And they are wonderfully dysfunctional.
At its heart, Dispatch is a workplace comedy wrapped inside a superhero adventure. The writing is easily one of its greatest strengths, balancing genuinely funny moments with a story about identity, failure, relationships, and second chances. But you aren’t just watching everything unfold. As emergencies appear across Los Angeles, you decide which heroes to send. Each team member brings different strengths and abilities, turning every call into a small strategic decision. Sometimes the obvious hero is unavailable, forcing you to improvise – and occasionally hope you haven’t just made everything considerably worse. Those moments help Dispatch stand apart from other narrative adventures. Your team isn’t simply a cast of characters you’re watching; they’re people you’re responsible for managing. And before long, I found myself genuinely caring about them. The game’s animated presentation only strengthens that connection. Dispatch often feels like you’re playing through an adult animated superhero series, backed by excellent performances from a cast including Aaron Paul, Laura Bailey, Jeffrey Wright, Matthew Mercer, and more.
What surprised me most, though, was the heart underneath all the chaos. Robert’s story asks an unexpectedly relatable question: When the thing you used to define yourself disappears, who are you without it? Come for the superheroes, questionable management decisions, and workplace chaos. Stay because somehow this dysfunctional team starts feeling like your own. Dispatch proves you don’t need to wear the cape to be the hero.
Same old story, right? Truck driver runs over office worker (Carissa) who’s immediately possessed by anime elf girl from the Isekai world of Talinfold. Destroy everything and everyone in your path with your truck to buff the elf’s power, but don’t forget your daily deliveries. If Carissa can defeat the Skeleton King she can open a portal home. Pretty simple.

sources.evidenceText:
Developer Frictional Games shares details of the first extended gameplay.
Ontos devs on the centered around a server of ratspsychological gameplay
After working on Ontos for over a decade, it is incredibly exciting to take a deep dive into the gameplay. Ontos is a spiritual successor to Soma, posing deep philosophical questions to players. Because of this, it is also always hard to figure out how to make it understandable in a short video. The focus of the game is not a tight, moment-to-moment gameplay loop, but a slower-paced experience of researching, testing, and eventually making a few critical choices. Now that we have a chance to showcase 10 minutes, it feels much easier to convey the intended feel of the game.
The main idea of the game is that you encounter complex experiments, each with its own setup, questions, and philosophical dilemmas. In this video, we get to see Crombie, who has been trapped in a computer server made of rats. Or at least that is what he says… As you can see in the video, the game starts by exploring nearby locations. These are often filled with information that helps you better understand the people and issues involved. In this case, there is even a small experiment, a strapped-in rat, that gives a taste of the difficulties to come. Here, players can test theories and make mistakes before encountering the main experiment.
Another early character is Zike – who we hear briefly over an intercom. Zike is a man seemingly obsessed with finding the soul. Understanding stuff like this is not just fun lore, but a critical part of the game. The better you understand how a character works, the more informed decisions you can make. Sometimes it is best to avoid certain questions or give answers contrary to your own feelings to achieve the intended results.
Once we enter the lab, we finally get the Rat Server revealed. I love this setup. Our thinking behind it was just to let a person be made from something that feels highly unlikely. Someone being simulated by a computer is not so hard to accept in this day and age. But by 60 rats strapped to a server rack? That is a harder pill to swallow. The hope is that these setups act as catalysts to other thoughts and questions. Are the rats conscious too? Can two conscious beings inhabit the same physical substrate? This is a good taste of what we want to provide in Ontos.
After you have met the Crombie (or the rat server, however you wanna feel about the situation), it is time for an experiment. You need to manipulate the probes on the Crombie’s head delicately. Now the player faces many options. You can follow the instructions or try other things based on things you’ve seen and read. The goal with all of this is to create a tense scene by mixing goals, unclear instructions, and always the risk of royally screwing it all up.
​The experiments can end in many ways, and it is never clear what your options even are. This also makes the game very replayable. The more you play, the more you understand, and the clearer the approaches will be.

sources.evidenceText:
The first demo for ONTOS revealed a game brimming with ideas and horrors alike - this spiritual successor to SOMA is shaping up beautifully.
ONTOS: This Horrifying, Tantalizing Thriller Feels Like an Immersive Sim for Puzzle Gaming
ONTOS is the kind of game you don’t stop thinking about, even after you’ve turned it off. And not just because it offers you the horrifying reality of the question: “What if a man’s consciousness was stored in a server rack made of rats?”
I’ve played its first demo – shown to press and creators at gamescom 2026 – several times already. The game itself is centered on Aditi, drawn to a seemingly abandoned moon resort-turned-science lab, Samsara by her estranged father. This demo is built around a single puzzle – get a key from one of the base’s scientists, Crombie. Sounds simple enough…
Like Frictional Games’ spiritual predecessor, SOMA , this game turns philosophical inquiry into weird science. Its characters are asking the big questions (‘What is the self? Are body and mind necessarily connected? What happens when I plug myself into The Rat-puter?’) and trying to answer them in increasingly grotesque ways.
But unlike SOMA , this isn’t built into the fabric of a traditional horror game. As far as I’ve seen, there are no stalking threats, no stealth – instead this is a game all about the puzzles you’re presented with, and the exploration in between. It almost skews closer to elements of immersive sims than it does a survival-horror, not least in how it lets you work out not just what you’re being asked to do, but how you want to do it.
In the case of Crombie, I’ve worked out how to turn off the server (R.I.P. rats) and bring his corporeal form back from the brink. I’ve also worked out how to take the copied consciousness and effectively overwrite Crombie’s original mind with its copy. And – just for science you understand – I’ve cut the server without doing either of those things and accidentally killed them both, letting me just slip the key from around his neck. That last one leaves me to wonder – can I effectively play ONTOS as the horror game villain?
The game lets me take any of these paths, with very little overt direction, and reacts to it seamlessly. I’m left to agonize over whether I’ve made the “right” choice – and it will be fascinating to see how other characters in this world will react when faced with them.
The reason I can’t stop thinking about ONTOS isn’t really because of the horrors and wonders it presents – it’s because I can’t stop my brain ticking over about how I could have engaged with them differently. There seem to be so many ways to solve a single puzzle. When spread out over the course of an entire game, that’s a massively intriguing prospect.
The problem is that Crombie’s copied his mind into the aforementioned rat contraption and become incapacitated. The key is hung around his neck, trapped beneath a mess of probes and wires inserted directly into his brain. I’ve replayed that single scenario multiple times because it’s not so much about finding the ‘correct’ solution as it is finding which solution you want to try.

Fable's game director Ralph Fulton spoke to us at gamescom 2026 about character customization and confirms: Yes, it's in there.
‘It’s Not a Revolutionary Thing for an RPG to Have’ — Fable Explains the Very Obvious Reason as to Why Its Hero Design Has Changed
Character creators are no new thing when it comes to video games, especially RPGs. Fable is just one in a very long line of adventures allowing you to sculpt a hero in your image, but when it comes time to showcase a game ahead of time, decisions need to be made.
Well, at gamescom 2026, the Forza Horizon studio revealed a new extended look at quest gameplay taking place in Albion’s capital of Bowerstone, in which the player hero took the form of a woman we hadn’t seen before. A response to online backlash or just a simple example of the variations available when playing around with Fable’s character creator? I asked game director Ralph Fulton.
Fable will launch on February 23, 2027, and you’ll have the freedom to make your character look however you like. It really is that simple.
From its initial reveal onward, we’ve become accustomed to seeing multiple chosen hero appearances throughout trailers and gameplay videos, of all shapes, sizes, and genders. But that first female hero is who has become the poster child for Playground’s reboot, with some people deciding it would be a perfectly normal thing to do to complain about her not being conventionally “attractive” enough.
“Earlier this year, we obviously revealed that we have had some customization in our game,” Fulton explains. “It's not a revolutionary thing for an RPG to have, but nevertheless, there was some speculation that we didn't, and we were happy to reveal: Yes, we did.”

「デモ版600万プレイ」3人マルチ爆弾解除『BOMBANANA!』、同接1万2000人の大盛況。「見ざる言わざる聞かざる」ドタバタ分担、要素大量で堂々の製品版
パブリッシャーのTARKは9月2日、Lefto Studioが手がける『 BOMBANANA! 』を配信開始した。対応プラットフォームはPC（Steam）。ゲーム内は日本語表示に対応している。本作は配信直後から賑わいを見せ、最大同時接続プレイヤー数は1万2000人を突破している。
『BOMBANANA!』は、「見猿」「聞か猿」「言わ猿」の“三猿”に分かれて爆弾解除を目指す協力型パズルゲームだ。3人は、それぞれ確認できる情報や利用できるコミュニケーション手段が異なり、必要な情報を仲間同士で伝えながら制限時間内の解除を目指す。プレイ人数は「3人固定」となっている。
本作は、3人が欠けた情報を補い合いながら爆弾を解除する、非対称な協力プレイが持ち味だ。爆弾を操作できても正しい手順が分からない、マニュアルを確認できても言葉では伝えられない、といった制約が役割ごとに設けられており、爆弾のパズルだけでなく意思疎通そのものが攻略要素となる。また、こうした3人によるコミュニケーションの仕組みや、役割ごとに異なる課題、製品版で増えたパズルモジュールなども評価されている。デモ版の段階で600万人以上を集め、製品版ではパズルやゲームモードを拡充された『BOMBANANA!』。今後どこまでプレイヤー数を伸ばすか注目したい。
『BOMBANANA!』はPC（ Steam ）向けに配信中。リリース記念セールとして、9月10日までは定価から38％オフの税込651円で購入できる。ゲーム内は日本語表示に対応している。
本作の特徴は、三猿をモチーフにした非対称な役割分担だ。たとえば「見猿」は、爆弾に直接触れて操作できる唯一の存在だが、目が見えないため、ケーブルの色や画面の表示を確認できない。「言わ猿」は、唯一、爆弾解除マニュアルを確認できるものの、言葉を発することができず、ジェスチャーなどを駆使して指示を伝えることになる。そして「聞か猿」は、爆弾の様子や仲間のジェスチャーを見ることができ、声を出して指示することも可能だが、ほかのサルの声が一切聞こえない。このように、マニュアルを読める者、操作する者、その間を取り持つ者に役割が分かれており、3人の情報を繋ぎ合わせなければ爆弾を解除することはできない。

開発者のLAirHisson氏は9月2日、『 PrismCraft 』を無料公開した。ブロックが三角形の『マインクラフト』風のゲームを自作したという。対応プラットフォームはPC（itch.io）。
『PrismCraft』は、『マインクラフト』に影響を受けたクラフトゲームだ。『マインクラフト』の世界が立方体のブロックで構成されているのに対して、本作では三角柱のプリズム（ブロック）が採用されているのが特徴。なお、公開されたバージョンでは『マイクラフト』のテクスチャは一切使用されていない。
本作にてプレイヤーは、底面が三角形のブロックを基本単位としたボクセルワールドにて、移動やブロックの破壊と設置など『マインクラフト』の基本的なゲームプレイを体験できる。三角形のブロックをグリッド状に綺麗に配置できることが特徴となっている。UIも三角形で表現されており、Eキーで開くインベントリでは、木から板や砂からガラスを作り出すといったことも可能。F5キーで三人称視点に切り替えると、キャラクターも三角形で再現されていることが確認できる。Tabキーではサバイバルモードとクラフトモードを切り替えることができ、三角形の世界で思う存分に建築を楽しめる。
本作を手がけるLAirHisson氏は、フランスを拠点とするYouTuber兼開発者だ。主に『マインクラフト』などのボクセルゲーム向けのModを制作し、動画として紹介している。同氏は10年以上『マインクラフト』をプレイしてきて、世界やキャラクターが立方体のブロックで構成されていることに疑問を抱いたという。そこで三角形の『マインクラフト』を自作することに挑戦したそうだ。
そして重要となるのが三角形の「形」だ。3Dブロックとしての三角形には、正三角形4面の正四面体や、立方体を真上から斜めに切断する直角三角柱などさまざまな形が存在する。LAirHisson氏は、底面が正三角形で側面が正方形となる三角柱「プリズム」を採用。『マインクラフト』における「ブロックの積み上げ」を実現しつつ、三角形の世界を構築するには、プリズム形状が最適と判断したという。
この段階では、空間のどこにでもプリズムを配置できるため、配置をグリッド状にスナップするよう「三角グリッド」の構築に移行。しかし、ここで大きな問題が発生する。『マインクラフト』のグリッドは正方形のため、ブロックをグリッドにスナップすればどこまでも綺麗に並べることができる。しかし、三角グリッドには「向き」が存在。単純にグリッドにスナップするようコーディングしただけでは、プリズムが毎回同じ向きに配置され隙間なく埋めることができない。LAirHisson氏は、上向きと下向きを交互に並べる処理に悩まされ、プロジェクトを作り直す決断を下すこととなる。

That day, Dothan Police school resource officers responded to reports of an altercation between a student under the age of 10 and a volunteer teacher at the Jerry Lee Faine Elementary School in Dothan, Alabama.

After 10 Years, Pokémon Go Is Getting a Pokémon Anime Crossover Episode
The world of Pokémon Go will cross over into the Pokémon anime series later this month, in an episode where the gang meet Professor Willow and spin a PokéStop.
Pokémon Go celebrated its 10th anniversary this summer, and the celebrations will continue this month as a landmark episode of the Pokémon Horizons series debuts in Japan on September 18, featuring a couple of very special guest stars.
Yes, Professor Willow himself will be making his anime debut, leaping over from his role assisting players in Pokémon Go. Coming along with him is Meltan, his partner Pokémon, and at least one PokéStop — the identifiers of real-world locations that Pokémon Go players spin in-game.

In a trailer posted today by the official Japanese Pokémon social media account, above Captain Pikachu can be seen spinning the PokéStop, accurately recieving Pokéballs and berries as a reward. And in a further nod, a Kecleon is revealed to have been hiding in plain sight — a neat nod to how the chameleon-like creature can be caught in Pokémon Go.
Exactly how Professor Willow will cross paths with Roy, Liko, and the series' other characters remains to be seen, as Go's canonicity with the rest of the Pokémon franchise has always been left unclear. Indeed, Meltan and Melmetal, which debuted first in Pokémon Go, lack an official region of origin (such as Johto or Kanto), and are instead listed as being discovered in an "Unidentified" place.
Regardless, Pokémon Horizons and Go will also crossover together within Pokémon Go itself, with the episode's Charizard wearing goggles available to catch in Go, as well as a return for Captain Pikachu. Another glorious day in the corps.
Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 Review So Far
Perhaps no movie was primed to be a video game more than Aliens. A bunch of marines with guns up against hordes of monstrous beasties? That’s a video game, baby. That was true for the first Aliens: Fireteam Elite, a game I enjoyed but didn’t stick with for too long, and it’s also true of its sequel, which freshens that returning structure up with things like an additional player and a new class. I’m not done with Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 yet (the joys of international travel to Gamescom, I reckon), but I’ve played enough to start laying down thoughts like one of my squadmates is spiriting for an objective and my words are covering fire. The short version is this: I’m having a good time with my friends, but I am curious how long we’ll want to play after the credits roll.
You don’t have to be familiar with the original to understand what’s up here: the USS Endeavor received a transmission from a very sick-looking woman named Dr. Pearce based on LV-558, a Weyland-Yutani mining colony overrun by Xenomorphs. The marines sent in Fireteam Banshee, an elite squad, to contain the situation. They’ve all gone missing. Your Marine has been transferred to the Endeavor to bring them home and figure out what the hell is going on.
What We Said About Aliens: Fireteam Elite (2021)
Aliens: Fireteam Elite does enough right to be plenty worthwhile for a trio of co-op shooter fans who’d rather battle hordes of xenomorphs than the usual zombies. Between the excellent weapons, classes, and enemy types and some wonderful nostalgic hat-tips toward what came before, it's a must-play if you hold any fondness for this series. The caveats, of course, are having to put up with repetitive scenarios and some excruciatingly drawn-out missions. Aliens: Fireteam Elite may not be a triumphant win, but it's far from a game over, man. - Kyle Campbell, August 23, 2021
Read the full Aliens: Fireteam Elite review .
The first game wasn’t huge on story, and it doesn’t bog down Fireteam Elite 2 either. Between missions, you’ll hang out on the Endeavor and chat with your squad. There’s Shipp, the Endeavor’s CO; Ko, your tough-as-nails, no-nonsense squad leader; Piper, an analyst who is new to boots-on-the-ground work and a little nervous as a result; Esther, the ship’s android; Raptor, your dropship pilot with terrible (and I do mean terrible ) jokes; and Wrench, your mechanic/weapons specialist/shopkeeper who dispenses rad bird facts.
I enjoy the crew, even if you only really interact with them from the waist up in very “look at their face while they talk to you” scenes. My only qualm is that, because they’re mostly just the voice in your ear on missions, there’s not much room for camaraderie – and when there is, everyone’s… too nice? One of the best parts of Aliens is that the characters don’t always get along, and while I think it’s great that Ko roasts Raptor (and you), I wish these characters razzed each other a bit more. It adds flavor, you know?

Andrew Garfield Historical Drama The Uprising Gets a Fortnite Crossover
Now available to play ahead of the film's release on September 10.
Nothing screams Fortnite like the Peasants' Revolt of 1381 , am I right?
Focus Features announced Wednesday that the new movie The Uprising , starring Andrew Garfield, is now available to play as a custom experience on Fortnite ahead of the Paul Greengrass-directed film’s theatrical release on September 10.
Even for Fortnite – which has a long history of pop cultural collaborations including Star Wars , Marvel , DC , LEGO , The Witcher , Godzilla and Kong , Stranger Things , John Wick , and Back to the Future – The Uprising is a curious film to see on this platform.
The period drama – which may or may not (still) be a Robin Hood origin movie – chronicles the Peasants’ Revolt of 1381, which was led by historical figures Wat Tyler (played by Shogun’s Cosmo Jarvis) and John Ball (played by Jamie Bell). Andrew Garfield’s lead character, Ploughman, is meant to represent the Everyman peasant pushed by misfortune into taking up arms against the crown.
According to the official announcement, “the free Unreal Editor for Fortnite (UEFN) experience, developed by Sawhorse Productions and published by Genesis Studios, immerses players in the heart of the legendary uprising, bringing the film's world to life through a large-scale multiplayer battle inspired by the events and visual landscape of The Uprising.”
“Set in 1380s England, the custom 5v5 payload-escort experience pits Rebels against Kingsmen in a battle for London’s gates. Rebel forces must push a battering-ram through four escalating map phases, advancing from muddy farmland to the fortified city walls, while Kingsmen fight to stop their advance before time expires. Players wield era-inspired melee weapons and bows, earn in-match currency and strategically upgrade their health, speed, and damage throughout the fight.”

Former Disney Interactive concept artist Ken Christiansen confirmed that Kingdom Hearts inspired a Smash Bros.-like crossover fighting game that never got off the ground.
Disney Was Working on Its Own Smash Bros.-Like Fighting Game, Confirms Ex-Concept Artist
In 2013, Christiansen posted a slew of artworks to his online portfolio , some of which showed rough sketches of various Disney characters facing off in battle. It sparked the idea that Disney had possibly toyed with a crossover fighting game — something that Christiansen has now confirmed.
Speaking with Time Extension in a September 1 interview, Christiansen opened up about the surprising way Kingdom Hearts helped bring the idea to life, though it ultimately never came to fruition. In fact, it was difficult for Kingdom Hearts to get approved in the first place, as Disney execs were hesitant to combine some of the brand’s most iconic properties.
"One of the reasons Kingdom Hearts was so difficult to get started was because Disney was so reluctant to have that possibility of crossing over The Lion King into The Little Mermaid world," he explained. "That was the main hangup for Disney America. They couldn't get over that. So, I think there was maybe just a little bit of butting of heads, but it all worked out in the end. All of the creatives, though — like me, the other artists, and the producers — we all thought it was the greatest idea in the world. Like, 'Yeah, let's cross over everything.'"
"Since Kingdom Hearts already kind of broke that mold, producers would say, 'Hey, what if we say they're action figures, and we kind of take the same conceit as Toy Story, but have them fight each other instead?' Then, we can have all these action figures of Disney characters from Tarzan, The Lion King, and Treasure Planet, and it can be this Smash Brothers kind of thing. The title of that concept was 'Disney's Action Figure Face Off."
Unfortunately, this game never came to be; Time Extension reports that the project only reached the prototype stage before Disney ditched the idea in favor of movie and TV tie-in games.
With this in mind, the concept art shared to Christiansen’s portfolio makes us even more wistful for this game that never happened. The artwork showed 1v1 battles between eight different characters: Captain Hook vs Beast, the Sheriff of Nottingham vs King Louie, Ursula vs John Silver, and the Queen of Hearts vs the Horned King. Some of these characters are seriously deep cuts (we’d never expect to see the Horned King in any major Disney offering these days, let alone the Sheriff of Nottingham), and it makes us wonder who’d get chosen if such a game were to actually get made in the modern day.

Final Fantasy Maker Square Enix Denies Rumors That It's Going Private
Final Fantasy developer Square Enix has spoken out to address rumors that it's going private.
Japanese business magazine Sentaku recently reported that Square Enix was looking into going private, leading to a nearly 12% increase in the company's stock price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange. But this is not the case, Square Enix has said, responding to the claim.
"The September issue of the monthly magazine Sentaku carried a report regarding the possibility of Square Enix Holdings Co., LTD. (the 'Company') going private. However, this information was not announced by the Company," Square Enix said in a statement . "No consideration is currently being given within the Company to taking the Company private."
The news comes amid wider consolidation across the gaming industry. EA was recently acquired by a Saudi Arabian investment group and taken private, which has led to concerns from both fans and EA employees about what its new owners will do. Will they continue to invest in single-player games from BioWare and leverage beloved IP like Dead Space, or will they go heavy on microtransactions and live-service games? It'll be a while before we can really see the effects of the acquisition and EA's decision to go private, but naturally, a report like this for Square Enix can lead to rampant speculation about the company's future.
Square Enix itself has made a lot of changes this decade, with arguably the biggest adjustment being when it off-loaded a lot of its western studios, such as Crystal Dynamics and Eidos Montreal, in 2022 . These teams were acquired by Embracer Group, meaning Square Enix no longer has the rights to franchises like Tomb Raider and Deus Ex. The company has also undergone multiple rounds of layoffs over the last few years, but has managed to soldier on.
